Job Title: Transmission Line Design Engineer or Engineer-in-Training 
 Job Level: ENG B/C/D ( We welcome applications from individuals with all levels of experience and will adjust the title and role accordingly) 
 Date Posted: July 13, 2026
 Closing Date: open until the position is filled
 Job Type: Full-time Permanent
 Category: Internal/External Opportunities 
 Location: Calgary
 Powering a bright future starts with you! 
 At AltaLink, people are at the heart of our success. We are a team committed to doing the right thing for each other and our customers. We foster an environment that is inclusive, collaborative and high performing and we value personal accountability. Our people are empowered to continuously improve, deliver outstanding customer service and make a meaningful impact every day. We embrace the unique identities, experiences and perspectives of our workforce, reflecting the communities where we operate. Everyone at AltaLink can expect to work in a safe, respectful environment where trust and commitment are at the core of how we operate. 
 Oh, and, what do we do? 
 We power Alberta! Our transmission lines deliver electricity to millions of Albertans 24 hours a day, seven days a week. When you’re on our team, you’re supporting Alberta’s homes, farms, businesses and industries by providing the safe, reliable and affordable electricity they rely on. Whether working in the field or in the office, every AltaLinker contributes to keeping the lights on. Want to join our team? We’re excited to share that we are hiring a Transmission Line Design Engineer.   
 Job Description: 
 An exciting opportunity currently exists for a “Transmission Line Design Engineer” within the Project Development – Lines & Civil Engineering Department at AltaLink. Reporting to the Manager, Lines & Civil Engineering.
 The successful candidate will be responsible for the design, engineering, project development and technical delivery of high voltage transmission line facilities across AltaLink’s transmission line network, from early scoping and conceptual development through detailed design, construction support, close-out and final acceptance. The individual will work closely with internal and external stakeholders to ensure line modifications, line rebuilds, customer interconnections, greenfield transmission line projects and urgent restoration work are designed and supported with a high level of quality, safety, constructability and customer service. 
 The position requires experience in project scoping, design, implementation, technical decision-making, construction support and final acceptance. The role also requires the ability to coordinate multi-stakeholder design inputs, manage design changes, support external EPC and contractor resources, and provide clear technical direction under tight project or field response timelines. As a senior designer on the team, the individual will provide guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and designers. This includes supporting technical development, coaching, design review, and knowledge transfer for emerging engineers and EITs. This position will appeal to individuals looking to apply extensive transmission line design experience and leadership talents in a dynamic utility environment.
 Responsibilities: 
 Prepare detailed calculations, studies, bills of material and design packages for transmission line capital, customer, Direct Assign and system projects.
 Prepare PLS-CADD models for design package development and existing line clearance evaluations.
 Complete line design packages for all AltaLink transmission voltage classes, including 69kV, 138kV, 240kV and 500kV assets, including rebuilds, modifications, greenfield lines, customer interconnections and emergency restoration work.
 Lead preliminary line design, route and structure option development, constructability review, material selection and design change resolution for complex transmission projects.
 Apply base geotechnical knowledge when developing line designs, including understanding soil classifications, borehole/geotechnical investigation outputs, groundwater/bedrock considerations, soil strength/deformation behaviour, frost depth, corrosivity data and backfill requirements as they relate to transmission line foundation selection and constructability.
 Support transmission line foundation design decisions for direct-embed poles, drilled shafts/caissons, screw/helical/bucket piles, driven piles, micro-piles, grillage and pad/footing applications, including review of compression, uplift, shear and moment reactions.
 Coordinate with geotechnical consultants, civil/foundation designers, project managers, construction resources and pile/foundation contractors to define geotechnical scope, review investigation results and resolve foundation design or installation risks.
 Consider foundation risk mitigation during design and construction support, including cave-in/sloughing risk, high groundwater, shallow bedrock, gravel/boulder interference, casing/culvert needs, washed gravel/backfill selection and impacts to schedule, cost, safety and reliability.
 Provide timely and effective technical input to support the Project Development and Execution teams.
 Develop scope descriptions for project estimating and provide clear implementation direction to internal designers, external engineering consultants, EPC contractors, construction resources and field crews.
 Review and/or approve technical drawings and specifications submitted by internal designers or contractors to ensure each project meets acceptable standards for operability, functionality, maintainability, reliability, durability and safety.
 Support construction execution and project close-out by resolving field questions, material issues, redline updates, design clarifications and as-built/return-data requirements.
 Support engineering standards development, design practice improvements and application of current or historical code requirements, including AEUC, CSA and applicable ISO reliability requirements.
 Provide subject matter support for line optimization, line rating, thermal rating, reconductoring assessments, facility applications, information requests and regulatory/hearing support as required.
 Contribute to material governance, supplier engagement, technical specifications, procurement support and emergency spare/material strategy for transmission line assets.
 Build and maintain effective working relationships with suppliers, external technical engineering resources, construction resources, customers and other stakeholders that results in growing understanding, good decisions and effective cooperation.
 Report on project engineering status to Project Managers and the Engineering Manager.
 Mentor junior engineers, EITs and designers through technical coaching, design reviews, knowledge sharing and support toward professional development.
 Provide leadership support within the team as required, including coordination of team deliverables, technical prioritization and coverage for management or project leadership needs.
 Maintain competency with current industry standards and regulatory groups such as AEUC, CSA and ISO Rules.
 Demonstrate key behaviors and meet identified expectations outlined in our four cultural pillars – one team, continuous improvement, customer focus and personal accountability.
 Qualifications: 
 Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Civil or Electrical Engineering.
 EIT or Professional Engineer with the Association of Engineers and Geoscientists of Alberta (APEGA) or qualifies for registration with APEGA.
 Transmission Line Design experience is considered an asset. 
 Proven ability to perform the responsibilities listed above. 
 Demonstrated experience delivering complex transmission line designs from concept through close-out, including coordination with project managers, external designers, contractors, suppliers and field stakeholders.
 Knowledge of standards and codes that apply to transmission line design and the ability to research and apply past code requirements to existing facilities in current situations, including Alberta power system facilities, Alberta Utility Code (AUC/AEUC) and Canadian Standards Association (CSA) requirements.
 Working knowledge of transmission line materials, structure families, insulator and hardware selection, conductor/OPGW applications, foundations, steel poles, wood poles and constructability considerations.
 Base knowledge of geotechnical investigation programs and geotechnical data used for transmission line design, including borehole/CPT information, soil classifications, soil strength and deformation behaviour, groundwater, bedrock, frost depth, corrosivity and backfill suitability.
 Base knowledge of transmission line foundation design and foundation reaction types, including compression, uplift, shear, overturning moment, lateral soil bearing, embedment depth, pile length/diameter considerations and pole/foundation deflection impacts.
 Ability to interpret geotechnical reports at a level sufficient to coordinate with geotechnical and civil/foundation specialists, identify design or constructability risks, and incorporate appropriate assumptions into line design packages.
 Experience in PLS-CADD and PLS-POLE is required.
 Experience using PLS-Tower, PLS-CAISSON, line rating tools, thermal rating methods, reconductoring assessments or line optimization studies would be an asset.
 Experience supporting customer interconnection, Direct Assign, Facility Application, AESO information request, regulatory/hearing or technical justification work would be an asset.
 Experience developing or applying engineering standards, technical specifications, material procurement requirements or supplier technical evaluations would be an asset.
 Experience with foundation-related standards, geotechnical scope development, foundation constructability reviews, or coordination of engineered foundation designs would be an asset.
 Superior organizational and time management skills, with the ability to manage a wide variety of projects/issues simultaneously.
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to work in a team environment with both office and field staff.
 Demonstrated ability to work under tight timelines and in high stress situations.
 Demonstrated mentoring, coaching or technical leadership experience with junior engineers, EITs, designers or cross-functional project teams.
 Must have a valid class 5 driver’s license.
 Ability and willingness to travel to site as required.
 Effective communication and interpersonal skills to interface with team members and customers to promote positive customer outcomes.
 Proven track record of good performance and attendance.

Global Privacy Strategy & DPO

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

Technical Consultants are on the frontlines working to establish partnerships with Ramp customers, and act as a liaison between customers and our internal technical teams. You'll be partnering with Customer Activation & Account Management teams to identify, prioritize and build financial solutions for new and existing customers so that Ramp continues to scale with their needs.

 

You will act as the technical and financial subject matter expert for our customers, and design solutions that address the customer's needs through Ramp and partner integrations. You will partner with Post-Sales teams to drive Product, Design and Engineering teams' roadmaps to evolve Ramp to better serve our customers at scale and offer increasingly higher value to the customers.

 

You will define the customer's financial & technical success criteria from onboarding through activation and expansion. You will represent Product, Design and Engineering externally and will operate with deep conviction and understanding of Ramp's technical capabilities. The role requires technical skills necessary to understand and educate on robust accounting features, and integrate them across all the touchpoints and surface area of a customer.

 

This role is specifically focused on Enterprise and Strategic Enterprise customers running Workday, supporting large, complex organizations with multi-entity environments, advanced ERP integrations, and highly customized financial workflows.

 - Serve as the primary Technical Consultant for Enterprise and Strategic Enterprise accounts running Workday, supporting complex, high-impact customers with multi-entity, multi-ERP, and global financial environments

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

Account Management

 - Identify opportunities for expansion across additional locations, brands, regions, and ownership groups.

 - Drive upsell, cross-sell, and multi-location rollout opportunities within existing restaurant accounts.

Market Insights

 - Serve as a strategic voice for the restaurant vertical by identifying emerging trends, influencing cross-functional priorities, and helping shape Solink’s long-term growth strategy within the industry.

 - Maintain a strong understanding of restaurant technology ecosystems, including POS, video security, payments, workforce tools, and operational platforms.

Restaurant Industry Expertise

 - Proven track record of exceeding quota and closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals.

 - Experience managing long sales cycles, pilots, procurement, legal review, and executive negotiations.

 - Ability to build strategic account plans and move large opportunities from prospecting to close.

Relationship Builder

 - Strong existing network within the restaurant industry.

 - Confident building trust with C-level executives, owners, operators, and functional leaders.

 - Skilled at turning relationships into qualified opportunities and long-term account growth.

 - Comfortable using industry events, referrals, and partner relationships to create momentum.

Strategic & Commercially Minded

 - Strong ability to identify high-potential accounts and understand where buying power sits.

 - Comfortable navigating franchisor, franchisee, corporate, and private-equity-backed restaurant structures.

 - Skilled at building ROI-driven business cases and aligning Solink to customer priorities.

 - Disciplined in qualification, forecasting, follow-up, and deal management.

Driven & Accountable

 - Competitive, self-motivated, and energized by building new business.

 - Consistent high performer with a desire to be at the top of the leaderboard.

 - Comfortable with travel for customer meetings, industry events, and strategic deal support.

 - Coachable, collaborative, and committed to continuous improvement.

 - Share industry expertise, enterprise selling strategies, and market insights with peers to strengthen team performance and contribute to the success of the broader sales organization.

Tool-Enabled & Process-Savvy

 - Experience using tools like SalesForce, Gong, ZoomInfo, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, and sales enablement platforms.

 - Strong pipeline hygiene, accurate forecasting, and clear next-step discipline.

 - Uses data, call review, account research, and sales process to improve performance.



NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience selling to large franchisee groups or multi-brand restaurant operators.

 - Existing relationships with QSR, fast casual, or casual dining brands.

 - Experience selling security, video, POS, payments, loss prevention, workforce management, or operations technology.

 - Familiarity with restaurant conferences, associations, franchise groups, or industry events.

TARGET CRUSHER

 - You are motivated by winning, energized by strategic enterprise sales, and excited by the opportunity to help Solink become the leading video intelligence platform for the restaurant industry.

 


SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

 - Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.

 - Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.

 - Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.

 


WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE HIRING PROCESS

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

 1. Intro Call with our Talent Team (45 minutes)

 2. Interview with the Hiring Manager (45 minutes)

 3. Final Presentation with Senior Leadership (60 minutes)

PLEASE NOTE: THIS IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE AT ANY POINT IN THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THE BUSINESS.

 


HOW TO APPLY

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our [Careers Page https://solink.com/careers/]. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

 


NOTICE: SOLINK USES ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) TO SCREEN, ASSESS, AND/OR SELECT CANDIDATES FOR THIS POSITION.




SOLINK IS AN EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER. WE’RE COMMITTED TO BUILDING A DIVERSE AND INCLUSIVE WORKPLACE. IF YOU REQUIRE ACCOMMODATION DURING THE SELECTION PROCESS, PLEASE LET US KNOW.

 Rabais pour les employés 
 Votre lieu de travail

L'entreprise produit également du fer et de l’acier destinés à des applications hautement spécialisées, notamment dans les domaines de l’industrie automobile et de l’énergie éolienne. Our purpose is finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs – striving for innovation and continuous improvement to produce materials with low emissions and to the right environmental, social and governance standards. We treat each other fairly and with dignity regardless of race, gender, nationality, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation or anything else that makes us different.
 À propos de Rio Tinto 
 Rio Tinto est un chef de file mondial du secteur des sociétés minières et des matériaux. Nous sommes établis dans 35 pays où nous produisons du minerai de fer, du cuivre, de l’aluminium, des minéraux critiques et d’autres matériaux nécessaires à la transition énergétique mondiale et à la prospérité des personnes, des communautés et des nations.

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to lead our Voice AI products. This is one of the fastest-growing line of business at Jobber and the clearest signal of where the company is headed next.

Jobber exists to serve small business owners—and our employer brand reflects that mission. Our customers are hard-working, hands-on entrepreneurs in industries like landscaping, HVAC, plumbing, and cleaning. They value reliability, speed, professionalism, and tools that help them work smarter and build stable lives for themselves and their families. Most are in the field, juggling priorities and relying on Jobber to keep their businesses moving. We care deeply about the real impact our product has on their day-to-day operations, their teams, and their communities.

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada's Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail's Canada's Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada's Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we've come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we've just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers.

The Product:

You’ll work across our rapidly-growing Communications products at Jobber. Receptionist, our headline Voice AI product, is the fastest-growing product at Jobber will be your primary focus. It’s the clearest expression of where we think this company goes next. In under two years it went from nothing to a multi-million dollar run-rate business, and today it answers thousands of calls a week for plumbers, cleaners, electricians, and landscapers who would otherwise have missed them. For a small home service business, a missed call isn't a missed notification. It’s missed revenue or a customer left in a lurch.

The Role:

You’ll lead the product strategy and execution for Jobber’s Voice products: products designed to help small service businesses to stay on top of their phone calls and keep their business moving even when they’re in a crawlspace or on a ladder.

We are looking for a product manager to take Receptionist from early, high-conviction customers to the majority of small businesses who could benefit from it.  Ultimately, you're building a business, not a feature. Jobber’s Voice product answers the phone and takes a message. Then it books the job, follows up on the quote, calls the customer back, and takes action inside Jobber on the service provider's behalf. Every new capability we ship is a new reason customers depend on us. You'll own the roadmap that takes us from receptionist to something much closer to an office manager.

The Product Manager will:

 - Turn Receptionist from a product early adopters love into one the majority of Jobber’s customers rely on daily.

 - Define and execute the roadmap for Receptionist and new Voice products balancing short-term wins with long-term innovation.

 - Deeply understand small business owners and office managers, synthesizing market, regulatory, and customer data into smart product decisions.

 - Prioritize user and business impact, ensuring every product decision drives value for Jobber’s small business customers.

 - Collaborate with domain experts across Voice AI, telephony and communications products to launch best-in-class products.

 - Act as the voice of the customer, especially for small business owners navigating an overflowing inbox.

 - Set the foundation for multi-product strategy, as we incorporate a full suite of communications and scale the business and team

To be successful, you should have:

 - Owned a revenue line — attach rate, pricing, or packaging — rather than engagement metrics alone.

 - Shipped (and improved) a production LLM or ML feature or product

 - Enough technical depth to be a real partner in architectural conversations about models, prompts, and pipelines.

 - Product management experience at a senior level, with evidence of shipping real things and seeing them through to long-term outcomes.

Highly desired (but not a deal-breaker) if you have:

 - A background in telephony or contact center technology — SIP, IVR, call routing, carrier and number registration.

 - Experience with consumer-facing conversational products

 - Familiarity with vertical SaaS, SMB, or home and field services.

 - Experience scaling products from 0 to 1 (and beyond)

Location:

We believe great collaboration is intentional, and sometimes that means coming together in person to build, brainstorm, and connect. To support this, the role is open to candidates based in one of our hub cities: Edmonton, Toronto, Vancouver, or Kitchener-Waterloo.

Compensation:

At Jobber, we believe that compensation should be transparent, fair, and reflective of your experience and growth. This role has a minimum annual salary of $145,900, a midpoint of $171,600, and a maximum salary of $197,400, designed to show the progression from learning the ropes to truly excelling.

We design our compensation to reflect each new hire's skills, experience, and against the complexity of the role, ensuring a fair and competitive salary. Our range is intentionally broad to support growth and long-term impact, with fully established hires typically starting around the midpoint. The higher end of the range is reserved for those who have demonstrated deep expertise and lasting contributions, while offers below the midpoint reflect strong potential with room to develop. This approach ensures that compensation aligns with both an individual's current capabilities and their opportunity for future growth.

Base salary is just one part of a total compensation package that will include equity rewards, annual stipends for health and wellness, retirement savings matching, and an extended health package with fully paid premiums for body and mind. Your professional growth matters to us, too! You'll have access to a dedicated talent development program that includes career coaching and opportunities for career development.

We believe in transparency and open conversations about compensation. If you have any questions about our approach, we're happy to discuss them throughout the hiring process!

What you can expect from Jobber:

 - A total compensation package that includes an extended health benefits package with fully paid premiums for both body and mind, matching in RRSP, TFSA or FHSA, and stock options.

 - A dedicated Talent Development team and access to coaching, learning, and leadership programs to help you grow your career, reach your goals, and unlock your full potential.

 - A unique opportunity to build, grow, and leave your impact on a $400-billion industry that has no dominant player...yet.

 - To work with a group of people who are humble, supportive, and give a sh*t about our customers.

We believe that diverse teams perform better and that fostering an inclusive work environment is a key part of growing a successful team. We welcome people of diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to working with applicants requesting accommodation at any stage of the hiring process.



A bit more about us:

Job by job, we’re transforming the way service is delivered. Your lawn care provider, home cleaning service, plumber or painter could use Jobber to better connect with their customers, save time in the office, invoice faster, and get paid! We’re bringing tens of thousands of people together with technology to deliver billions of dollars a year in services to happy customers. Jobber exists to help make these small businesses successful, and when they’re successful we all win!

ABOUT SOLINK

At Solink, our mission is to safeguard what matters most. We provide businesses with the tools to know sooner and act faster by transforming video security into real-time operational insights.

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Technical Accounting Manager to be our go-to person on technical accounting research, keeping our accounting policies current, and assisting with complex transaction accounting for the company. This role is distinct from the core close/consolidation function — it's focused on getting the judgment calls right: revenue recognition for complex or bundled hardware/software arrangements, new accounting pronouncements, and one-off or non-routine transactions. You'll report to the Assistant Controller and act as the internal technical resource for the rest of the accounting and finance operations team, as well as a key liaison to external auditors on complex matters.

Given our hardware-enabled SaaS model and multi-entity structure reporting under IFRS, this role has real scope for meaningful technical work — multi-element revenue arrangements, lease accounting, share-based payments, and financial instruments, among others.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Research and document technical accounting positions on complex or non-routine transactions (e.g., multi-element hardware/SaaS bundled arrangements, contract modifications, new product launches).

 - Draft accounting memos supporting judgment areas under IFRS (e.g., IFRS 15 revenue recognition, IFRS 16 leases, IFRS 2 share-based payments, IAS 36 impairment).

 - Monitor new and amended IFRS pronouncements, assess impact on the business, and lead implementation efforts.

 - Partner with Legal, Sales, and Product teams to review new contract structures and advise on accounting implications before deals close.

 - Work with the Assistant Controller to review technical accounting policies and ensure they are documented, current, and consistently applied across all legal entities.

 - Act as the primary point of contact for auditors on technical accounting matters and complex areas of judgment.

 - Support M&A due diligence and purchase accounting, if applicable.

 - Partner with the Assistant Controller on the practical application of technical positions during the close process.

 - Provide training and guidance to the broader accounting team on technical topics.




ROLE EXPECTATIONS

This is a P4 level role. At Solink, individuals at this level are established contributors who work independently within their area of expertise while receiving general direction from their manager.

In this role, you'll be expected to:

 - Serves as the go-to resource for IFRS interpretation on complex, non-routine transactions for the accounting team and the entire organization

 - Drafts technical accounting memos and position papers with minimal oversight

 - Evaluates new revenue arrangements, leases, or financial instruments for accounting treatment

 - Own Solink’s accounting policy manual

What success looks like:

 - Solink accounting policy manual is completed and up to date

 - Clean and efficient annual audit process

 - Solink prepared well in advance of any accounting changes impacting financial reporting




WHAT YOU BRING

Must-Have

 - Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance or related field; CPA or CA required (or in progress).

 - 3-5 years of accounting experience, including public accounting (Big 4 or large regional firm) experience strongly preferred.

 - Deep working knowledge of IFRS, with particular strength in revenue recognition (IFRS 15) and other judgment-heavy areas.

 - Comfortable using AI tools to accelerate research and first-draft memo preparation, with rigorous review and professional judgment applied before finalizing any position.

 - Experience with multi-element or bundled revenue arrangements — hardware/software combined offerings a strong plus.

 - Strong technical writing skills; ability to produce clear, well-supported accounting memos.

 - Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-accounting stakeholders (Sales, Legal, Product).

Preferred Experience

 - Exposure to IFRS reporting.

 - Experience working directly with external auditors on complex accounting matters.

 - Experience in a hardware-enabled SaaS or similarly complex revenue environment.

 - Experience with multi-entity, multi-currency reporting structures.

 - Experience leading new accounting standard implementation projects.




SECURITY REQUIREMENTS

 - Candidates must undergo a criminal records check upon hire;

 - Be a Canadian Citizen (dual citizens included), or eligible to work in Canada;

 - Be willing to comply with Solink’s own security policies and standards.




OUR VALUES

We do things the Solink way:

 - Act with URGENCY – Our customers move fast, so we do too.

 - Deliver with QUALITY – We sweat the details and hold a high bar.

 - Win with TEAM – No egos. Just outcomes, built together.

 - Lead with TRUST – We earn it through clarity, consistency, and care.
   

These aren’t just words—they shape how we hire, lead, and grow.




WHY SOLINK?

We’re not just building tech - we’re building a place where great people do great work.

 - Clarity and trust: Where the role allows, we support flexibility in how and where work gets done - and we’re upfront about what’s required.

 - Meaningful equity: Every full-time, permanent employee has a stake in our growth.

 - Comprehensive benefits: Fully paid health & dental (no waiting period) + $500 health spending account.

 - Wellness support: Monthly reimbursement for fitness, wellness, or mental health programs.

 - Growth through merit: Advancement is based on contribution, initiative, and the ability to raise the bar - together.

 - Candid culture: Clear expectations, honest feedback, and no politics.

 - Social connection: From So-learns to Solink-o and So-lunches, we stay connected in ways that actually feel fun.




WHAT TO EXPECT FROM THE HIRING PROCESS

We respect your time and value transparency. Here’s a general idea of what to expect:

 3. Role-Relevant Task or Case Study (if applicable)

PLEASE NOTE: THIS IS SUBJECT TO CHANGE AT ANY POINT IN THE RECRUITMENT PROCESS BASED ON THE NEEDS OF THE BUSINESS.




HOW TO APPLY

Submit your resume and a short cover letter via our Careers Page https://solink.com/careers/. Let us know what excites you about this role, and how you’d help move Solink forward.

As a Security Engineer on the Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team, you’ll help build and scale programs that support commercial audits, federal compliance, security risk management, vendor risk, policy management, and customer trust. You’ll be expected to identify opportunities where AI can improve GRC workflows and turn useful experiments into practical, reliable solutions. How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. • Work with GRC platforms such as Drata, Tines, Vanta, ServiceNow, Archer, LogicGate, Secureframe, or comparable tools, and use automation techniques such as APIs, scripts, webhooks, ticketing workflows, and cloud or identity integrations.

Digital Transformation Strategy Implementation Specialist 
 The Work 
 As a Manufacturing Strategy Specialist, you will work with clients to quickly assess their manufacturing and operational environments, identify improvement opportunities and develop practical recommendations and transformation roadmaps, and then stay with the work through to implementation. This role suits someone who is as comfortable on the plant floor as in the boardroom. You can hold your own in a strategy discussion with client executives, but a framework or a slide deck doesn’t satisfy you. You want to see the recommendation running on the line and delivering real results.
 Key responsibilities include:
 Conduct rapid, hands-on assessments of manufacturing facilities and operational environments, spending time on the floor with operators, supervisors and engineers, to identify performance gaps, risks and improvement opportunities.
 Develop broad-based recommendations to improve manufacturing performance, operational efficiency, productivity, cost, quality and sustainability.
 Work with clients to understand their priorities and translate those priorities into actionable manufacturing and operations strategies.
 Develop transformation roadmaps, value cases, business cases and implementation plans aligned with client objectives.
 Stay engaged beyond the roadmap, working through implementation detail with client and delivery teams so that recommendations are realized in practice.
 Facilitate strategy discussions and working sessions with client executives, operational leaders and cross-functional teams.
 Analyze manufacturing processes, operating models, organizational capabilities and performance data to identify opportunities for meaningful improvement.
 Bring a current, informed view of emerging manufacturing technologies, such as AI, industrial IoT, automation, advanced analytics and digital twins, and help clients understand where they can create real value.
 Support the design and delivery of large-scale manufacturing and operations transformation programs.
 Apply Accenture’s methods, tools and assets to support assessments, strategy development and transformation delivery.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams across strategy, consulting, engineering, technology, operations and client account teams.
 Identify and help mitigate risks associated with transformation initiatives.
 Monitor project progress and support the timely delivery of key milestones and client outcomes.
 Communicate findings, recommendations, project status and business value to senior client stakeholders.
 Contribute to business development activities, including client proposals, solution development and transformation opportunities.
 What Sets You Apart 
 You have a genuine thirst for new technology. You follow developments in AI, IoT, automation and digital manufacturing because you find them fascinating, and you explore them on your own: tinkering and reading up on how things actually work.
 You’re a doer and a strategist. You can operate and discuss at a strategic level, but you’re energized by getting into the detail, whether that’s the data, the process or the practical challenges of making change stick.
 Some of your best days at work have been spent in steel-toed boots. If a client offers a plant tour, you’re first in line, and you’ll have a dozen questions for the operators by the end of it.
 You challenge the status quo. You bring a healthy dose of skepticism, whether to “the way it’s always been done” or to the latest technology hype. You ask the hard questions, test assumptions with data, and push clients to aim higher than incremental improvement.
 Your Experience Counts 
 Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in manufacturing, operations, strategy consulting or a similar role.
 Experience assessing manufacturing facilities or operational environments and developing broad-based, actionable recommendations.
 Manufacturing or operations industry experience, with an understanding of manufacturing processes, performance drivers and operational improvement opportunities.
 Experience facilitating client discussions and working with senior stakeholders to define priorities and transformation strategies.
 Experience developing transformation roadmaps, business cases or value cases for manufacturing or operational improvement programs.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to quickly evaluate complex operational environments.
 Ability to convert assessment findings into practical recommendations and implementation plans.
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Operations Management, Supply Chain Management or a related discipline.
 Experience supporting or delivering transformation, operational excellence, process improvement or performance improvement initiatives.
 Strong written and verbal communication, presentation and facilitation skills.
 Ability to work across multidisciplinary teams and manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced consulting environment.
 Valid passport and ability to travel within Canada, the US and internationally.
 English is required for this position as this role will be aligned to multi-national teams where English is the common language across our North America Market. Due to the significant high volume of interactions with these English-speaking multi-national teams, which is inherent to this position, it is not possible to reorganize the company's activities to avoid this requirement.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Previous experience working for a consulting firm or in an internal strategy, operational excellence or transformation role.
 Experience working across multiple manufacturing environments or industry sectors.
 Knowledge of manufacturing strategy, operational excellence, lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, digital manufacturing or Industry 4.0 concepts.
 Experience developing executive-level presentations, assessment findings and strategic recommendations.

 This site-based role is in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and requires periodic international business travel, including travel to the United States. The Vice President is a member of the PDM Manufacturing Leadership Team and partners across the Global Manufacturing network to shape enterprise strategy and deliver shared business outcomes.
 Responsibilities: 
 Lead the Edmonton Site Leadership Team and align directly managed and matrixed functions around clear priorities, decision rights, performance expectations, and shared accountability for site outcomes.
 Translate enterprise and Global Manufacturing priorities into medium- and long-term site strategy, annual operating plans, resource requirements, and measurable performance objectives.
 Ensure site operations are executed safely, compliantly, reliably, and efficiently to meet product demand, quality, service, cost, and financial commitments; establish management routines that enable timely decisions and transparent accountability.
 Build and develop a high-performing, inclusive, feedback-rich leadership team; strengthen succession pipelines and critical capabilities; and foster an environment in which employees are included, developed, empowered, and accountable.
 Establish a culture and management system of operational excellence and continuous improvement, using data, digital capabilities, automation, and new technologies to improve safety, quality, reliability, productivity, cost, and speed.
 Sponsor transformational change, simplify and scale processes, and build cross-functional commitment to new capabilities and ways of working.
 Provide strategic oversight for clinical and commercial drug-substance manufacturing, packaging, analytical testing and release, maintenance, engineering, supply chain, technical operations, scale-up, technology transfer, registration, and product launch activities at the Edmonton site.
 Contribute to CMC strategy, governance, and decision-making for the commercial portfolio through active partnership with PDM product teams and functions including Quality, Technical Development, CMC Regulatory, Product Strategy, PDM Strategy and Operations, and Global Supply Chain.
 Ensure inspection readiness and sustain compliance with applicable cGMP, health, safety, environmental, employment, legal, fiscal, and statutory requirements.
 Develop and manage operating and capital budgets, capacity plans, workforce plans, and investment priorities in alignment with site and network requirements.
 Establish proactive business-continuity and risk-management plans that protect employee safety, regulatory compliance, product supply, critical operations, and site service commitments.

 Provide technical and strategic support to internal and external cGMP manufacturing and testing operations.

 What This Role Actually Looks Like
 We invest heavily in growing your caseload through marketing, client matching, and a strong referral engine.  Hours

 Potential for schedule growth, based on your availability and our demand.

 Excellent communication skills (both written and verbal), including the ability to work effectively with others and cultivate strong relationships across functional teams.

The Opportunity
 We're Optix – and we're building a future where great spaces run themselves
 At Optix ( optixapp.com ), we build software that automates bookings, billing, access and member communication for coworking and flexible-space operators. Our ambition is fully autonomous, human-centred flexible spaces – where the business can run around the clock and the people behind it have more time to welcome members, make introductions and bring their communities together.
 Operators in 25+ countries already use Optix. Our roots are in coworking, and customers such as Le Birdie , a 24/7 self-service golf venue, are showing how much further the idea can travel. We see an opportunity to change what owners believe is possible: the hours they can open, the experiences they can create and the businesses they can build.
 If you want to be at the forefront of how AI and automation transform the way people run and experience physical spaces, then this is where you'll do it.
 The Role
 Your first-year goal is to double the number of businesses Optix serves. You'll define and prove the acquisition channels that deliver it, while keeping acquisition costs sustainable relative to customer lifetime value.
 You'll own marketing strategy and performance: deciding who we target, how we position Optix and where we invest. You'll lead the existing marketing team and build it along the way, staying hands-on with acquisition experiments, advertising and conversion. You'll own hiring and budget allocation alongside the CEO.
 Operators will arrive with a booking problem, and leave with an idea for a business they hadn't thought possible. You'll show operators how Optix could help them run and grow their businesses, and give them a reason to choose us.
 Whether this is your first opportunity to lead marketing or your next business to help build, you'll have a meaningful part in defining our direction. As Optix grows, you should be able to see your judgment, creativity and leadership in the company we become.
 What You'll Do
 • Set the growth strategy – decide which operators to prioritise and how we'll grow our share of the market.
 • Shape our position – define positioning, product messaging and thought leadership that show coworking and flexible-space operators what they can build with Optix.
 • Develop acquisition channels – run structured experiments, improve the channels that work and build a sustainable way to reach the right operators.
 • Improve conversion – work with sales on lead quality, demo bookings, trial enrolments and the journey from trial to paying customer.
 • Lead delivery and learning – set priorities for the team, review the work and report marketing performance and recommendations to leadership.
 • Own advertising and investment – direct digital advertising, manage marketing budgets and use data to balance acquisition returns with long-term brand development.
 • Own marketing measurement – define funnel metrics and put reliable tracking and reporting in place, from first interest to paying customer. Use customer, revenue and acquisition-cost data to guide strategy, evaluate experiments and decide where to invest.
 Compensation & Details
 • Annual salary $130,000–$150,000 CAD
 • Location Vancouver, BC, with three days a week in the office
 If you're a marketer who combines imagination with commercial judgment and wants to help shape how an industry grows – we'd love to meet you.

WHY HARVEY

At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.

This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.

Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.

At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.


FUNCTION OVERVIEW

Harvey's Legal Engineering team is composed of former practicing attorneys who work to bring value to Harvey's prospects and customers. Legal Engineers lead discovery, demos, trainings, and onboarding alongside our AEs and CSMs. They translate real legal work into Harvey solutions, serving as the trust layer across the entire customer lifecycle, from the first pilot to the most complex, custom-built workflow.



At Harvey, we segment the Legal Engineering function into three teams: Legal Engineers (Pre-Sales), Legal Engineers, Product Specialists (Post-Sales), and Legal Engineers, Custom Solutions (Pre- and Post-Sales). Legal Engineers across all three subgroups understand how lawyers think and work, and use that expertise to design, build, and refine solutions that hold up under live in-practice pressure. In doing so, they don't just drive adoption; they shape Harvey's product roadmap, ensuring every release is grounded in what the legal profession needs. It's a team built to power Harvey as the platform lawyers can trust with their most important work.

 

You may be asked to travel around 2-3+ times per month. Travel is always for a significant business need and typically is for 1-3 days at a time.





WHAT YOU'LL DO

Legal Engineer (Pre-Sales)

Legal Engineers are lawyers who left practice to help build the future of legal work. Working closely with Account Executives, they engage with many of the world’s leading law firms and legal teams throughout the pre-sales process. They lead collaborative pilot programs, guide prospects through what’s possible with AI, and work alongside lawyers to understand their workflows, build tailored solutions, and demonstrate meaningful value in real legal use cases. Along the way, they bring prospect feedback back into the product, helping shape the future of Harvey.

 

Legal Engineer, Product Specialist (Post-Sales)

LEPS take over once a prospect becomes a customer. LEPS build trusted relationships with many of the world's leading legal teams by learning their workflows and showing them how to weave Harvey into daily practice.  The LEPS role spans the entire customer journey, from leading onboarding and enablement, to sitting down with a full practice group to build agents on real matters. Along the way, the LEPS translates legal practice needs into actionable feedback for product and engineering, contributes to customer-facing content across practice areas, and upholds Harvey's credibility as the leading AI platform for lawyers.

 

Legal Engineer, Custom Solutions (Pre-Sale and Post-Sale)

LECS are a specialist group that work on complex no-code custom Harvey in-app solutions. LECS meet with group heads, general counsel, and other senior stakeholders to learn how key processes run today. Drawing on their legal expertise, they use natural language prompting to design bespoke resources, including agents, playbooks, and other tools, that improve the quality, speed, and experience of that process. The build is collaborative. The LECS scope it with the customer, prototype against sample documents, and refine it alongside their team. Most LECS work happens post-sale, but the team also supports strategic accounts pre-sale on an advisory basis. LECS concentrates narrowly on designing tools that automate a specific process, and on building relationships with the senior leaders who own it.

 

*In your initial interview with our recruiting team, you'll learn more about all three roles, and we'll identify which may be the best fit based on your background and our current hiring needs.


What You Have

You move confidently through uncertainty, you operate at speed, and ship solutions that work—iterating quickly with lawyers, sales teams, and product partners to help Harvey and its customers win. You bring deep curiosity about AI's potential to transform legal work, a bias toward action, and the creativity to solve problems nobody's cracked yet.

 - Deep understanding of corporate legal workflows (e.g., commercial contracting, governance, compliance, or transactions) and curiosity about how AI can reshape them.

 - Proven ability to navigate business-oriented legal environments, balancing legal risk with practical commercial outcomes.

 - Demonstrated ability to exercise sound judgment and make confident, well-reasoned recommendations in fast-paced, ambiguous settings.

 - Ability to operate seamlessly across legal, product, and sales contexts—translating between stakeholders with clarity and precision.

 - Executive presence and strong relationship-building skills, with experience engaging business stakeholders, senior leadership, and cross-functional partners.

 - Experience working cross-functionally with product, sales, or business teams in an in-house setting; customer-facing or business development experience is a plus.

 - French speaking is a plus.

A profitable DTC pet brand is looking for a Head of Retention & Customer Experience to join our team! You will own everything after the first order: subscriptions, email and SMS, the post-purchase journey and customer experience, across both of our brands.
 We're doing $50M+ a year and scaling to $100M+, and we want one senior leader who owns retention A-Z: lower churn, significantly higher lifetime value and a better customer experience across the board. We are looking to hire someone with 5-6+ years in retention or lifecycle at DTC brands, who has led retention at a subscription brand doing $30-50M+ a year (ideally nine figures). The ideal candidate is hands-on in Klaviyo and Loop (or similar), has led a retention and customer experience team, and has managed agencies.
 The mission of this role 
 Own retention A-Z to fuel the growth to 9-figures. This role comes in to drive three things: lower churn, significantly higher lifetime value, and a better customer experience across the board. Success is lower churn, stronger retention, much higher lifetime value, more revenue from email and SMS, and happier customers.
 Who are we? 
 We are a profitable DTC brand selling premium pet products. We sell across Shopify, Amazon and Chewy, and we're one of the fastest-growing brands in the pet space – $50M+ in annual revenue and scaling to $100M+. We recently launched a second brand, expanding into a new customer base. We're a 100% remote, lean, senior team that moves fast, and every person here has a massive impact on the business.
 What is our culture like & who is a good fit? 
 Culture-fit is our #1 factor when hiring! We have a genuine will-to-win. No work is beneath us if it moves us towards our goals. We use creativity to do more with less – and quickly. We use data to make decisions and live by four core values:
 Better Everyday: have a retention test live every week across subscriptions, flows or the post-purchase experience, and write down what each result teaches.
 Speed Is King: spot a churn, refund or CSAT problem the day it shows up and have a fix in motion that week.
 Work Smart: AI and automation first. Claude reads cancellation reasons, reviews and tickets to find why customers leave, AI drafts flow copy and segments, and retention KPIs report themselves every week.
 Overdeliver: bring the CEO the next big retention lever before being asked, and get more lifetime value from every customer than the plan called for.
 If you want a stress-free corporate 9–5 job, this isn't it. 
 If you want to challenge yourself and shape a fast-growing company, work directly with the founder, and play a big role in scaling it to $100M+... If you want to drive results with a group of passionate, smart, hardworking people, in an environment without politics or corporate chicanery, being hands-on and active – then you've come to the right place.
 Outcomes (what success looks like) 
 90-day targets for each outcome are agreed with you before your start date.
 Churn goes down: monthly subscription churn and save rate, by brand
 Retention improves: repeat purchase rate and cohort retention at 3, 6 and 12 months
 Lifetime value rises significantly: 12-month lifetime value by cohort and brand vs the same cohorts last year
 Email and SMS drive more revenue: email and SMS share of total revenue, and revenue per recipient
 Customers are happier across the board: CSAT, review rating, refund rate and tickets per order
 Key Objectives 
 Own the subscription program for both brands: offers, cadence, bundles, the customer portal and the cancellation flow.
 Build and test save offers, skip, swap and pause options, and win-back flows to cut churn.
 Own email and SMS strategy for both brands, and manage the retention agency's calendar, flows, targets and results.
 Build the lifecycle journey from first order to loyal customer: welcome, post-purchase, replenishment, cross-sell, win-back and VIP flows.
 Map and improve the full post-purchase journey, and run a loyalty, referral or VIP program if the numbers support it.
 Lead the customer experience team and set customer service policy that protects both the customer and the margin.
 Report cohort retention and lifetime value against target every month, and name the biggest lever.
 Fully remote, based outside the US.
 Fluent in English.
 Retention Leadership: 5-6+ years in retention or lifecycle at DTC brands, including leading retention at a subscription brand doing $30-50M+ a year (ideally nine figures). This is a must.
 Subscription Expertise: you have grown a subscription program and know churn, saves, cohorts and MRR inside out.
 Lifecycle Marketing: you build email and SMS programs (Klaviyo or similar) that drive a large share of revenue without burning the list.
 Tools: deep hands-on experience with Klaviyo (or similar) and Loop (or a similar subscription platform).
 Analytical: you read cohort, lifetime value and churn data fast and find the lever that moves the number.
 Testing Discipline: you run clear tests on offers, flows and save tactics, and read results honestly.
 Leadership: you have led a retention and customer experience team, including managing agencies, through KPIs and goals.
 Commercial Judgement: you protect margin, and know when a discount or save offer earns its cost.
 Customer obsessed: you understand why customers stay or leave, and fix the cause, not the symptom.
 Excellent cultural fit as per our values above.
 Excited to play a big role in scaling the company and work closely with the founder.
 Accountabilities 
 What you own. Each one is checked green, yellow or red every week.
 Subscriptions and churn: own the subscription program for both brands, keep at least one save or retention test live every week, grow the share of new customers who subscribe (working with the CRO Lead on on-site and post-purchase offers), and report subscribers, MRR, churn and save rate by brand every week.
 Email, SMS and lifecycle: own email and SMS strategy, manage the retention agency, keep the calendar live and flows in testing, keep list health and deliverability strong, and plan sale and launch campaigns with the Head of Growth and the Head of Brand & Community.
 Post-purchase experience and loyalty: ship at least one post-purchase improvement every month, and use cancellation reasons, reviews, surveys and support contact reasons to find why customers leave and fix the cause with the owning team.
 Customer experience and support: lead the Customer Experience Manager, own the weekly CX KPI scorecard (CSAT, first response time, AI resolution rate, refund rate and chargebacks), set customer service policy, and grow 4- and 5-star reviews.
 Retention data and reporting: track cohort retention, repeat purchase rate and lifetime value by brand and channel, report retention KPIs weekly, run a monthly retention review with the CEO, and write the retention playbook as SOPs so it runs without one person.
 How Our Hiring Works & How We Operate 
 (1) Application + Screening Interview
 (2) In-Depth Interview with our CEO
 (3) Reference Calls
 (4) Final Interview with our CEO
 Salary Expectation 
 USD $115,000 to $145,000 a year (based on experience and expertise) + performance bonus of 15-20% of base after the trial period.

Nous aidons les entreprises dans leur croissance numérique dans les domaines de la gestion de l'expérience client, du contenu d'entreprise, de la communication client et du contenu structuré.
 Notre client, un leader de l’industrie aérospatiale, est à la recherche d’un(e) Product Owner / Analyste d’affaires pour contribuer à la réussite de ses projets et assurer l’alignement entre les besoins d’affaires, les équipes techniques et les utilisateurs finaux.
 Le rôle de Product Owner / Analyste d’affaires est essentiel pour traduire les besoins des parties prenantes en exigences claires et réalisables. À la croisée des affaires et des technologies, la personne titulaire du poste contribue à définir la vision du produit, à prioriser les besoins et à assurer la livraison de solutions qui répondent aux objectifs de l’organisation.
 Elle agit comme intermédiaire entre les parties prenantes, les équipes de développement et les utilisateurs finaux, tout en favorisant la collaboration et l’amélioration continue dans un environnement de travail agile
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 Vision & Stratégie du Produit : 
 Agir en tant que principal point de contact entre les parties prenantes (entreprise, clients et équipes de développement).
 Recueillir les avis, les retours et les exigences des propriétaires d'entreprise, des clients et des autres parties prenantes pour s'assurer que le produit répond à leurs besoins.
 Organiser des sessions régulières de retour d'information et de révisions avec les parties prenantes pour garantir l'alignement.
 Développer et maintenir une feuille de route décrivant les fonctionnalités du produit, les améliorations et les livrables.
 Documentation des requis et Gestion du Backlog : 
 Créer des documents de requis d’affaires et fonctionnels détaillés.
 Créer, maintenir et prioriser le backlog produit, en veillant à ce qu'il soit clair et réalisable pour l'équipe de développement.
 Rédiger des histoires utilisateurs détaillées, définir les critères d'acceptation et garantir la clarté des exigences.
 Prioriser en continu les tâches en fonction de la valeur commerciale, de la demande du marché et de la faisabilité technique.
 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes de développement, y compris les ingénieurs logiciels, les concepteurs et les testeurs, pour garantir une compréhension partagée des exigences et des priorités.
 Participer aux cérémonies agiles telles que la planification des sprints, l'affinage du backlog et les revues de sprint.
 Assurance Qualité et Tests : 
 Collaborer avec les parties prenantes pour définir les critères d'acceptation. Veiller à ce que les fonctionnalités livrées respectent les normes de qualité et les attentes des utilisateurs.
 Effectuer des tests d'acceptation utilisateur (UAT) pour valider que les solutions livrées répondent aux exigences commerciales et aux besoins des utilisateurs.
 Amélioration Continue : 
 Surveiller les indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) et les retours des utilisateurs pour identifier les domaines d'amélioration et d'optimisation.
 Identifier de manière proactive les opportunités d'améliorer les processus, les outils et les méthodologies afin de stimuler l'efficacité et l'efficience.
